articles.full_text:
Odisha has ordered all government, aided and private schools, along with Anganwadi centres, to stay shut in six districts from November 19 to 21.
November 19, 2026 / 08:26 IST
Cyclone Akvan Tracker: Regional Meteorological Centre, Kolkata
Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan over the west-central Bay of Bengal is moving north-northwestwards and is likely to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri around noon on Friday, November 20, with sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting up to 110 kmph, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
Railways have rescheduled three trains because of the cyclone:
- 18046 Charlapalli-Shalimar East Coast Express: Now leaves at 3.40 pm on November 19, instead of 8.40 am
- 12704 Secunderabad-Howrah Falaknuma Express: Now leaves at 5.55 pm on November 19, instead of 3.55 pm
- 15227 SMVT Bengaluru-Muzaffarpur Express: Now leaves at 8.30 am on November 19, instead of 12.30 am
Odisha shuts schools, red warning in 13 districts
Odisha has ordered all government, aided and private schools, along with Anganwadi centres, to stay shut in six districts from November 19 to 21.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said on Wednesday that the state was fully prepared and had started taking the necessary steps. A red warning has been issued for 13 districts, he said.
“According to the Meteorological Department, the cyclone is expected to make landfall on the 20th, between Narsapur in northern Andhra Pradesh and Puri,” Majhi said after a review meeting at the State Control Room.
He said heavy rain is likely across several districts, with winds averaging around 100 kmph.
“There is a high probability of heavy rainfall, particularly in districts across southern Odisha and the coastal belt—extending as far as Balasore—including Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, and Kalahandi,” he said.
“We have held discussions with the District Collectors regarding the comprehensive management and response strategy for the impending cyclone. The state government is fully prepared and has already begun taking measures to address the situation,” he added.
The Indian Navy and other agencies are also coordinating their preparations as authorities track the storm. (With ANI inputs)
